title: Psalm 43: Send Out Your Light and Your Truth
summary: A worshiper far from the temple asks God to take up his case against deceitful and unjust people. He cannot understand why God seems to have rejected him, and he asks for God's light and truth to lead him back to the holy mountain and the altar. The psalm closes with the same refrain that runs through Psalm 42: a man talking to his own downcast soul and telling it to hope in God.

from.where: The Study Bible's notes on Psalm 43
from.text: The psalm is an individual lament

line: The end of the poem begun in Psalm 42: a prayer for God's light and truth to lead him back to the altar, and the refrain again, telling his downcast soul to hope in God.
guide: If you read Psalm 42 and stopped, read this one too; the refrain is the same, but now he faces forward and asks to be led. Notice the name he gives God in verse 4, and pray it before the way back has opened.

stanzas.title: A plea for justice and a question about rejection
Light and truth to lead the singer back to the altar

verses.t: Vindicate me, O God, and plead my case against an ungodly nation; deliver me from deceitful and unjust men.
For You are the God of my refuge. Why have You rejected me? Why must I walk in sorrow because of the enemy’s oppression?
Send out Your light and Your truth; let them lead me. Let them bring me to Your holy mountain, and to the place where You dwell.
Then I will go to the altar of God, to God, my greatest joy. I will praise You with the harp, O God, my God.
Why are you downcast, O my soul? Why the unease within me? Put your hope in God, for I will yet praise Him, my Savior and my God.
